idea-plugin.name: Guiced
idea-plugin.description:
Guiced is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin based on the JetBrains Guice plugin, providing full Google Guice and GuicedEE 2.3.0 framework support for IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2+.

☕ Support this plugin: Buy me a coffee on Patreon

GuicedEE Framework Support

  • Create new GuicedEE projects with proper Maven dependencies
  • Generate module-info.java files with required dependencies
  • Create service loader implementations
  • Create various GuicedEE component templates:
    • Guice Modules
    • Lifecycle Hooks (Pre-Startup, Post-Startup, Pre-Destroy)
    • REST Services (with optional service class and DB session)
    • Router Configurations
    • Persistence / Database Modules
    • Cassandra Modules
    • MongoDB Modules
    • Redis Modules
    • HTTP Proxy Modules
    • WebSocket Channels, Message Receivers, and Hooks
    • RabbitMQ Connections, Consumers, and Publishers
    • Kafka Consumers
    • IBM MQ Consumers
    • Vert.x Startup and Configurators
    • Classpath Scanner SPIs
    • Cloud: Runtime Environment Providers, Service Registry Providers, Status Change Listeners
    • Consul and Consul Service Resolver support
  • Application templates for different use cases
  • Identify GuicedEE applications in the Services window
  • Recognise @VertxEventDefinition methods and classes as framework entry points so event-bus consumers are not flagged as unused

GuicedEE guice-core — Enhanced Google Guice

Upstream policy: this module tracks Google Guice releases and carries documented GuicedEE extensions for JPMS, annotation SPIs, and local dependency scoping. Local scoping follows the proposal in google/guice#1949.

  • Full JPMS module — ships a real module-info.java (module com.google.guice) with explicit exports, requires, and uses directives
  • JDK 25 compatibility — access-level and reflection fixes so Guice runs cleanly on the module path without --add-opens hacks
  • Jakarta namespace — uses jakarta.inject and jakarta.annotation (not javax.*)
  • SPI-driven extensibility — six ServiceLoader-based SPIs let you register custom annotations for injection points, scopes, bindings, and naming without touching Guice source
  • Multibindings built-in — MapBinder, Multibinder, and OptionalBinder are included in the same module (no separate guice-multibindings artifact needed)
  • Drop-in replacement — all public Guice APIs remain unchanged; existing @Inject, @Provides, @Singleton, bind() EDSL code works as-is

Install via Maven:

<dependency>
    <groupId>com.guicedee.modules.services</groupId>
    <artifactId>guice</artifactId>
</dependency>

SPI Extension Points (com.google.inject.gee)

Six SPIs loaded via java.util.ServiceLoader — declare uses in the Guice module and provides in your own module to extend Guice's annotation handling at runtime:

SPIPurpose
InjectionPointProviderRegister custom annotations that mark injection points (beyond @Inject)
InjectorAnnotationsProviderDeclare additional annotations that Guice should treat as injector annotations
BindScopeProviderProgrammatically bind custom scope annotations during module configuration
ScopeAnnotationProviderSupply scope meta-annotations used to recognise concrete scope annotations (for example, jakarta.inject.Scope)
BindingAnnotationProviderSupply annotation classes to be recognised as binding annotations (like @Named)
NamedAnnotationProviderMap custom naming annotations to Guice's @Named, enabling alternative naming strategies

Local scopes on injected dependencies

GuicedEE allows a scope annotation on an injected constructor parameter or field. Locally scoped providers are shared by the consuming constructor or field group, scope annotation, and dependency key. Other consumers remain isolated, and any existing binding scope stays underneath the local wrapper. Method-injection and provider-method parameters retain their existing behavior.

@Inject Handler(@RequestScoped RequestState state) { ... }
@Inject @RequestScoped RequestState fieldState;

Define custom scopes with runtime retention and @ScopeAnnotation, including PARAMETER and FIELD targets. Bind the concrete annotation to a Scope with Binder.bindScope() or a BindScopeProvider. Register that provider through JPMS provides or META-INF/services on the classpath. An unregistered scope fails injector creation.

For an alternative scope meta-annotation, register its marker type through ScopeAnnotationProvider; the concrete scope still needs a binding. The application owns request entry, exit, and asynchronous context propagation.

What Changed from Upstream

AreaChange
Module descriptorAdded module-info.java with full exports, requires, uses
Jakarta namespacejavax.inject → jakarta.inject, javax.annotation → jakarta.annotation
Access levelsWidened select internal access modifiers so packages work under strict JPMS enforcement
com.google.inject.geeNew package with 6 SPI interfaces for pluggable annotation handling
MultibindingsBundled into the core module instead of a separate artifact
Guice internalscom.google.inject.internal exported for framework-level consumers
Local dependency scopingConstructor parameters and injected fields can apply scope annotations around an existing binding

Full Google Guice Support

  • Templates for creating Guice modules, providers, binding annotations, scope annotations, and method interceptors
  • Coding assistance: inspections, intentions, line markers, and navigation
  • Navigate between injection points and bindings (explicit bind() and JIT bindings)
  • 18 Guice-specific inspections for common mistakes
  • Intention actions to move bindings and scopes to class annotations
  • Works with both Google Guice and GuicedEE guice-core dependencies
  • SPI-driven injection point recognition — fields annotated with @Endpoint (REST Client) or @ConfigProperty (MicroProfile Config) are treated as injection points, with full implicit usage detection, gutter icons, and click-through navigation
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.3.0

  • Generated Maven and Gradle projects use GuicedEE and test BOMs 2.3.0
  • Local dependency scope support for injected constructor parameters and fields
  • Scope conflict inspections recognise custom scope annotations; lifetime inspections include local request and session scopes
  • Scope annotation templates include type, method, parameter, and field targets
  • Guice documentation explains consumer-local caching, wrapped binding scopes, and scope SPI registration

2.2.0

  • GuicedEE 2.2.0 baseline — generated projects now reference com.guicedee BOMs 2.2.0 (Vert.x 5.1.5, Jackson 3.2.1, Hibernate ORM 7.4.3)
  • GraphQL instrumentation fix — the GraphQL module now combines the Vert.x future and JSON object adapters through a single ChainedInstrumentation, so both instrumentations apply instead of the second silently replacing the first
  • GraphQL dependency hygiene — GraphQL-Java's embedded (shaded) Guava copy is stripped and rewired to the canonical com.google.common module, removing duplicate Guava, tracking central Guava CVE fixes, and producing a clean JPMS graph
  • Telemetry — 3 new endpoints — the telemetry module now supports 3 new endpoints, with its underlying dependency upgraded to the latest version
  • Vert.x entry-point recognition — methods (and classes) annotated with @VertxEventDefinition are now treated as framework entry points, so event-bus consumers are no longer reported as unused code
  • Hibernate ORM 7.4.3 + Hibernate Reactive 4.5.1 — the two are version-locked to each other; the BOM now pins hibernate-maven-plugin and hibernate-processor to the same ORM build so enhanced bytecode and generated static metamodels always match the runtime
  • Security updates — pgJDBC 42.7.13 and SCRAM 3.4 (CVE-2026-54291 / CVE-2026-53712), Jackson 3.2.1 (CVE-2026-59889) and Spring 6.2.19 (CVE-2024-22233); Bouncy Castle 1.85
  • Deterministic BOM resolution — the GuicedEE BOMs no longer emit Maven 4 "Ignored POM import" model problems, which previously made dependency versions depend on import order and could break Maven project import in the IDE

2.1.0

  • Cloud support — Service Registry, Consul, Consul Service Resolver, and Azure Container Apps options in project wizard
  • Cloud intentions — Quick-add @ServiceRegistryOptions, @RegisteredService, and @AzureContainerApps annotations to package-info
  • IBM MQ intention — Quick-add @IBMMQConnectionOptions annotation
  • Verticle intention — Quick-add verticle scaffolding to classes
  • Queue Publisher intention — Inject QueuePublisher fields via quick assist
  • Annotation dialog — Unified "Add Annotation" dialog for all package-info annotations
  • Platform update — IntelliJ Platform 2025.2.6.1 baseline (sinceBuild 252)
  • Gradle Plugin — IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin updated to 2.5.0
